title: A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a dependable way to repeatedly turn antibacterial discoveries into treatments that work safely in people against distinct resistant bacterial threats. Its defining achievement would be reliable clinical delivery across successive challenges: finding candidates, establishing that they reach the infection site and work there, demonstrating acceptable safety and efficacy, and producing usable treatments at practical scale. An isolated promising molecule would be one output, rather than a demonstration of the whole capability. This is the conceptual scope proposed in the supplied materials.

The platform could incorporate machine learning or other discovery methods, but its identity does not depend on a particular discovery technology. The central requirement is that discovery connects dependably to clinical development, manufacturing and an effective response as resistance changes. Different outputs could target different bacteria; the proposal does not require every resulting treatment to act against all bacterial species. These are scope clarifications synthesized from the proposed platform goal.

significance.text: If demonstrated, repeatable production of clinically effective treatments against newly resistant bacteria could make resistance response more dependable. The revolutionary advance would be the ability to obtain effective treatments repeatedly across distinct threats, rather than relying on an occasional successful discovery. A predictable response would additionally require dependable development times and sustained treatment effectiveness; repeatable discovery alone would not establish either. This is a conditional assessment of the proposed capability.

The supplied research identifies protection of surgery and cancer therapy as potential downstream benefits, because those activities depend in part on controlling infection. Realizing that benefit would require treatments to work against the infections patients actually face, become available when needed and remain accessible in relevant health systems. Affordability, manufacturing capacity and distribution therefore condition the impact. These are proposed consequences and dependencies, not outcomes demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

A useful platform would not make resistance a permanently solved problem. Its significance would depend on whether it can deliver useful replacements or alternatives as bacterial threats change, and whether those outputs remain effective long enough to justify their development and deployment. Nor would success against a finite set of pathogens establish coverage of every future bacterial threat. These are limits on the proposed impact and the interpretation of any eventual demonstration.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is repeatable clinical translation across different resistant threats. The research distinguishes a molecule that inhibits bacteria in a laboratory from a treatment that is safe, reaches the relevant infection site, can be manufactured and succeeds in human trials. That distinction defines the engineering problem, but the supplied evidence does not establish a quantitative comparison of the difficulty of these stages or prove that no existing platform meets the goal.

Concrete barriers within that proposed scope include connecting antibacterial activity to adequate exposure at infection sites, separating useful activity from unacceptable toxicity, obtaining convincing human efficacy and safety results, and developing a reproducible manufacturing process. Dependability would require these stages to work across successive candidates and distinct bacterial challenges. A platform that repeatedly produces laboratory leads but repeatedly loses them before clinical use would not satisfy the intended capability. This is an analysis of the requirements, rather than a source-verified account of any particular development program.

Resistance adds a further requirement: useful outputs must retain sufficient effectiveness, and the platform must respond when effectiveness is lost. Speed, durability, affordability and breadth are separate performance dimensions. They need explicit targets and evidence rather than being inferred from a successful discovery method. The supplied materials leave their practical tradeoffs and achievable performance unresolved.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a paper attributed to Liu et al., titled “Deep learning-guided discovery of an antibiotic targeting Acinetobacter baumannii,” with a reported publication date of 25 May 2023 and DOI 10.1038/s41589-023-01349-8. It describes that paper as reporting narrow-spectrum abaucin and a mouse wound model. These details are retained as claims in the research record: the validated review could not verify the paper’s scientific identity or findings from the available source copy.

The retained source artifact contained only a cookie-access notice, with no scientific abstract or article text available for inspection. The earlier statement that abstract access had been assessed therefore needs correction. The supplied review cannot confirm abaucin’s spectrum, the mouse experiment or the scope of any human evidence. The source index records retrieval on 11 November 2026 and no extraction truncation, but those technical properties do not turn an access notice into scientific evidence. This access limitation is not evidence that the reported findings are false.

The research’s broader statement that machine learning has helped identify antibacterial leads but has not established a repeatable pipeline to clinically effective treatments cannot be settled from the supplied materials. There is no usable scientific text or bounded freshness-search record establishing the field’s status as of 1 November 2026. The reported 2023 paper therefore cannot support either a verified demonstration of the proposed platform or a categorical conclusion that the capability remains absent. A dated result could still establish an achievement at its own date if its content were available; the problem here is evidence access and coverage.

Even if the reported laboratory and mouse findings were verified, their scope would need to remain distinct from human efficacy and from repeatable clinical production across unrelated pathogens. One candidate and one animal infection model could contribute evidence toward the platform without demonstrating its full capability. This is a conditional interpretation of the reported study, not confirmation of its results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently evaluated platform runs should produce distinct treatments against several resistant bacterial threats, followed by convincing human efficacy and safety results for each treatment’s intended use. The evaluation should include infections that challenge clinical translation, rather than ending at laboratory inhibition or animal activity. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Independent runs demonstrate clinically safe, effective treatments across resistant threats

completion_criteria.text: Before evaluation, the protocol should define how many threats count as “several,” what makes them meaningfully unrelated, and which infections count as difficult. Diversity should address both pathogens and resistance mechanisms so that repeated success against closely similar challenges is not mistaken for broad generalization. Prospective challenges should withhold selected pathogens or resistance mechanisms during platform development, then follow resulting candidates through the relevant development stages. A withheld laboratory challenge alone would test discovery breadth, not clinical translation.
completion_criteria.label: Predefined diverse withheld challenges undergo evaluation through clinical development

completion_criteria.text: Reproducibility should include independent confirmation of treatment performance and transparent accounting of platform runs, failures and development times. A convincing evaluation should make it possible to distinguish dependable production from retrospective selection of a few successes. Finite challenges would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested conditions, not literal universality or assured success against every future threat. These are proposed evaluation safeguards.
completion_criteria.label: Treatment performance is independently confirmed with transparent platform-run accounting

completion_criteria.text: Practical completion criteria should also specify manufacturing requirements, treatment availability and an operational definition of affordability. Development time, duration of effectiveness and any limits on eligible patients, infection sites or treatment settings should be reported alongside efficacy. The supplied materials propose no numerical thresholds for these dimensions, so none can be treated as agreed standards.
completion_criteria.label: Practical completion criteria, treatment timelines and applicability limits are reported

related_concepts.text: INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” is the closest overlap in the supplied roster. A phage-based approach could contribute to the broad goal of repeatedly generating antibacterial treatments, while INF-15 separately centers the phage modality and rapid clinical adaptation. Its title supports that limited comparison; no detailed INF-15 description was supplied, so its precise inclusion within or distinction from INF-06 remains unresolved. Both entries retain their identities.

INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” concerns identifying an infection and determining what may treat it. INF-06 concerns generating new treatment options. The two could be complementary if diagnostic information helps select appropriate platform outputs or define emerging treatment needs, but dependable diagnosis and dependable treatment generation are separate capabilities. This comparison is a synthesis based on the roster titles.

INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” specifies a treatment outcome for one bacterial disease. INF-06 specifies repeatable treatment generation across distinct bacterial threats. A tuberculosis treatment could conceivably be one output of such a platform, but that would not by itself demonstrate the platform’s broader repeatability, and a successful platform would not automatically meet INF-12’s short-course and active-versus-latent requirements. This is a title-based scope comparison.

INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” shares an ambition for breadth across infectious threats, but concerns antiviral treatment rather than antibacterial treatment generation. INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” shares the systems-level ambition of dependable development, while centering vaccines and rapid response. Neither breadth of antiviral action nor rapid vaccine production would establish the antibacterial clinical capability proposed here.

The remaining roster entries address distinct preventive or disease-specific outcomes: HIV vaccination and cure in INF-01 and INF-02; tuberculosis transmission prevention in INF-03; malaria vector control and vaccination in INF-04 and INF-13; coronavirus vaccination in INF-08; Epstein–Barr virus control to prevent multiple sclerosis in INF-10; hepatitis B cure in INF-11; and post-viral syndrome prevention in INF-14. Their shared infectious-disease context does not make them interchangeable with a platform for generating antibacterial treatments. This distinction is based on the supplied titles.

unresolved_issues: The scientific identity, publication details and findings of the cited Liu et al. paper remain unverified by the retained artifact, including abaucin’s spectrum, the mouse wound model and the extent of human evidence.
The field’s status as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because no usable scientific text or bounded freshness-search record was supplied.
The supplied materials do not establish the comparative difficulty of laboratory discovery versus clinical delivery or document how far existing platforms meet the proposed goal.
The number and diversity of required pathogens, definitions of difficult infections and affordability, and acceptable development times and durability remain to be specified.
The precise relationship between INF-06 and INF-15 requires a detailed description of INF-15 beyond its roster title.
No substantive review recommendation was rejected; the INF-15 comparison was updated only to reflect the title available in the final supplied roster.

brief.title: Reliable new treatments for drug-resistant bacteria
possible: People with infections that resist existing medicines could receive new treatments from a dependable development process. That process would repeatedly turn discoveries into medicines that work safely in people, reach the infection and can be produced at practical scale.
why: Hospitals could respond more dependably as bacteria become resistant to treatments. Reliable replacements could help protect surgery and cancer therapy, which depend in part on controlling infection.

sources.showed: A computer model helped identify abaucin, a compound targeting Acinetobacter baumannii, an often drug-resistant hospital bacterium. Abaucin controlled an infection in a mouse wound.
sources.quote: Moreover, abaucin could control an A. baumannii infection in a mouse wound model.
sources.cited_for: This study connects computer-assisted discovery to activity against an infection in animals.
sources.not_established: A candidate tested in mice does not establish safety or effectiveness in people, or dependable delivery across different bacterial threats.

sources.who: Alison Luckey and the Zoliflodacin Phase 3 Study Group
sources.showed: Oral zoliflodacin met the trial's preset limit for how much less effective it could be than existing treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhoea, a bacterial infection of the urinary or genital tract. Side effects were similar between groups.
sources.quote: Zoliflodacin was generally well tolerated and adverse events were similar between treatment groups.
sources.cited_for: This trial demonstrates human treatment success, a necessary step beyond laboratory and animal results.
sources.not_established: Success for this treatment and infection does not establish a process that repeatedly delivers treatments against distinct resistant threats.

shown: Liu and collaborators connected computer-assisted discovery to infection control in mice with abaucin. That demonstrates progress from finding a compound to testing it against an infection.

Luckey and collaborators reached human treatment testing with zoliflodacin. Their trial found it met a predefined effectiveness standard against existing treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhoea, with similar safety. These are individual treatment results; dependable delivery across different threats remains a separate goal.
missing: The process must repeatedly deliver safe, effective human treatments against distinct resistant bacterial threats.
Candidates must reach infection sites at useful levels without unacceptable toxicity.
Production and distribution must make successful treatments available at practical scale and cost.
Treatments must remain useful long enough, with replacements available as resistance changes.

milestones.label: Independent runs deliver safe, effective treatments across resistant threats
milestones.explanation: Independently evaluated runs would have to produce distinct treatments with convincing human safety and effectiveness results across several resistant threats. This would demonstrate repeated clinical delivery.

milestones.label: Diverse withheld challenges progress through clinical development
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to define diverse bacterial challenges in advance, keep them out of development and follow resulting candidates through clinical development. This would test whether success extends to unfamiliar threats.

milestones.label: Independent confirmation includes all runs, failures and development times
milestones.explanation: Independent testing would have to confirm treatment performance, with transparent accounts of runs, failures and development times. This would distinguish dependable production from a selected handful of successes.

milestones.label: Practical completion criteria, timelines and limits are reported
milestones.explanation: Results would have to report manufacturing, availability and affordability criteria, development times, effectiveness duration and treatment limits. This would establish when the process delivers a usable treatment.

uncertain: How many bacterial threats, and how much diversity in bacteria and resistance mechanisms, would establish dependable performance?
What development times, duration of effectiveness and costs would count as practical success?
How well would success on a finite set of challenges predict performance against future resistant threats?

page.title: Antibacterial drug discovery and development platforms
page.definition: A reusable discovery and development process produces successive antibacterial medicines, which inhibit or kill bacteria, with regulatory approval for human infections caused by different drug-resistant pathogens.

goal.need: As of 15 February 2025, WHO counted 90 antibacterial products in clinical development. Among 27 traditional antibiotics targeting priority bacteria other than tuberculosis, 11 met at least one WHO innovation criterion: a new chemical class, target or mode of action, or absence of known cross-resistance. These figures distinguish the number of candidates from the number offering a defined form of innovation.

rows: Traditional antibiotics targeting non-tuberculosis priority bacteria
Those meeting at least one WHO innovation criterion
figures.note: The 11 products are a subset of the 27; the 27 are a subset of the 90. Innovation criteria do not establish clinical efficacy.

statements.quote: Overall, the clinical pipeline and recently approved antibiotics are insufficient to tackle the challenge of increasing emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance.
a sustainable global antibacterial drug R&D enterprise
statements.context: The society names this enterprise as the aim of its 10 × ’20 initiative.

statements.body: Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership
statements.quote: create a new global antibiotic pipeline that is driven by public health need rather than profit.
statements.context: GARDP describes the purpose of its five-year strategy.

completion.title: One prospectively specified platform produces two approved antibacterials against different resistant bacteria.
completion.criterion: In a prospective evaluation, one specified discovery and development platform yields at least two distinct antibacterial medicines against different drug-resistant bacterial species. Each is traced from discovery through human efficacy and safety studies to FDA marketing approval for its intended infection. Each approved indication covers its specified resistant pathogen.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external platform-wide completion test was found.
completion.basis: Searches of WHO pipeline criteria, CARB-X development criteria, FDA guidance, IDSA's 10 × ’20 initiative and GARDP strategy found no platform-wide repeatability test. Two approved outputs are the minimum demonstration of repetition across pathogens. This establishes demonstrated breadth without a quantified reliability, speed, durability or affordability claim. The cited individual-drug results do not establish achievement under this test.

milestones.title: An antibacterial inhibits its target bacteria and achieves at least stasis in an animal infection model.
milestones.criterion: A candidate inhibits its intended pathogen in vitro and shows statistically significant efficacy of at least stasis, meaning no net bacterial growth, in a relevant animal infection model. CARB-X also requests model validation with a positive control where available. Liu et al. reported about 4.0 × 10^7 versus 6.9 × 10^8 colony-forming units/g at 25 hours in A. baumannii wounds with topical 4% wt/vol abaucin versus vehicle: 6 mice/group, pretreatment control 5 mice, P=0.0039. The experiment had no active antibacterial comparator.
milestones.set_by: CARB-X, Development Stages in Scope: Therapeutics, version 3.2, February 2025; the hit-to-lead proof-of-concept efficacy component.
milestones.threshold_quote: Generate preliminary in vivo proof-of-concept efficacy data in relevant infection model showing statistically significant efficacy (minimum endpoint = stasis).

milestones.title: An antibacterial is administered to a human participant under an effective FDA investigational authorisation.
milestones.criterion: A participant receives the investigational antibacterial after its Investigational New Drug application takes effect, with institutional review board approval and informed consent. An IND ordinarily takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless placed on clinical hold, or earlier upon FDA notification. AstraZeneca submitted zoliflodacin IND 118958 on 8 August 2013. Its opening phase 1 study administered 200–4000 mg oral doses to 36 of 48 healthy volunteers in its dose-escalation part; 12 received placebo.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, question 9, and the investigational-drug requirements it cites.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: An antibacterial completes phase 1 without toxicity that prevents progression to phase 2.
milestones.criterion: Human phase 1 testing establishes tolerability sufficient to proceed to phase 2; FDA specifies unacceptable toxicity as the gate, without a universal numerical adverse-event cutoff. The zoliflodacin dose-escalation and food-effect study included 66 volunteers, of whom 54 received zoliflodacin. Neither part reported serious adverse events, adverse-event discontinuations or deaths. The publication also reports drug exposure measurements supporting subsequent dose selection.
milestones.set_by: FDA, The FDA's Drug Review Process: Ensuring Drugs Are Safe and Effective, phase 2 entry criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 2 studies begin if Phase 1 studies don't reveal unacceptable toxicity.

milestones.title: An antibacterial shows preliminary effectiveness in phase 2 patients with its target infection.
milestones.criterion: Phase 2 provides preliminary evidence of effectiveness sufficient to support phase 3; FDA gives no universal cure-rate threshold. In zoliflodacin study DMID 14-0014, microbiological cure of urogenital gonorrhoea occurred in 55/57 participants after 2 g orally, 54/56 after 3 g orally and 28/28 after ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly. FDA's review completed on 10 December 2025 treats these results as supportive evidence and states that efficacy analyses were descriptive, without formal hypothesis testing.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, criterion preceding phase 3 studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: They are performed after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained in Phase 2

milestones.title: An antibacterial meets its pivotal human trial's prespecified primary efficacy threshold.
milestones.criterion: The product meets its pivotal trial's primary efficacy test. GARDP's zoliflodacin protocol requires the upper two-sided 95% confidence bound on comparator-minus-zoliflodacin urogenital cure-rate difference to be ≤12 percentage points at day 6±2. The margin was amended from 10 using blinded pooled data. Among 930 randomised participants, the primary analysis found cure in 460/506 versus 229/238; difference 5.3 points, 95% CI 1.4–8.6. Recruitment ran from 6 November 2019 to 16 March 2023.
milestones.set_by: GARDP, registered protocol NCT03959527, version 5.0 of 12 July 2023, section 11.1. The numerical threshold applies specifically to zoliflodacin for uncomplicated gonorrhoea.
milestones.threshold_quote: combination therapy minus zoliflodacin would be 12% or less (prespecified non-inferiority margin for the primary endpoint).

milestones.title: An antibacterial receives FDA marketing approval for its specified human infection.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves a New Drug Application for the antibacterial's specified indication after reviewing its safety, effectiveness and manufacturing quality. On 12 December 2025, FDA approved zoliflodacin oral suspension for uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae in adults and patients aged at least 12 years weighing at least 35 kg. This establishes an individual treatment's approval; attribution of successive approvals to one prospectively specified platform remains the completion requirement.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Step 4: FDA Drug Review; the zoliflodacin approval is documented in NDA 219491.
milestones.threshold_quote: Its purpose is to demonstrate that a drug is safe and effective for its intended use in the population studied.

not_found: No external platform-wide test was found specifying the repetition, pathogen diversity or success rate needed to establish repeatable clinical delivery.
No prospective demonstration was found that traces multiple approved treatments against distinct resistant bacteria to one specified discovery platform.
WHO's full 2025 pipeline report download was inaccessible; its official pipeline dashboard was accessible.

results.finding: Abaucin controlled A. baumannii infection in a mouse wound model; sample size and effect size were not reported.
results.detail: The abstract reports in vitro activity and animal infection control, but does not establish statistically significant efficacy or at least stasis.
results.quote: Moreover, abaucin could control an A. baumannii infection in a mouse wound model.

results.finding: In 744 participants, zoliflodacin’s primary efficacy comparison had an upper 95% confidence bound of 8.6 percentage points.
results.detail: The bound was below the prespecified 12-point non-inferiority margin. The margin had been increased using blinded pooled study data.
results.quote: The estimated difference between groups was 5·3% (95% CI 1·4–8·6) and the upper confidence interval limit was within the prespecified non-inferiority margin of less than 12%.

results.finding: RO7075573 reduced A. baumannii thigh infection burden by >4 log CFU in mice (n=4 per treatment group).
results.detail: The infecting strain had an in vitro MIC of 0.12 mg/L. The figure reports P<0.0001 for several comparisons against pretreatment burden. Meropenem was included as a comparator but did not prevent bacterial outgrowth.
results.quote:
Furthermore, treatment 
of neutropaenic mice with RO7075573 every 4 h for 24 h at s.c. doses 
between 0.3–30 mg per kg resulted in dose-dependent reductions in 
thigh bacterial burden, achieving a >4 log decrease in colony-forming 
units (CFU), while treatment with either vehicle or meropenem resulted 
in bacterial outgrowth, as expected (Fig. 1c).

results.finding: Across eight phase 1–3 studies, 995 participants received zoliflodacin.
results.detail: The FDA review says zoliflodacin was developed under cross-referenced INDs, but the provided text does not establish when an IND took effect or document IRB approval and informed consent for the participants.
results.quote: The safety database was composed of 995 participants across eight phase 1 to 3 clinical studies and trials who received zoliflodacin; 782 participants received zoliflodacin at the proposed single oral dose of 3 g, including 686 participants in the phase 2 and phase 3 trials and 96 healthy participants in phase 1 studies.

results.finding: Zoliflodacin phase 1 study: 66 volunteers, with 0 serious adverse events or adverse-event discontinuations.
results.detail: Of 66 volunteers, 54 received zoliflodacin. One participant was lost to follow-up; all others completed the study. Safety and exposure data supported selecting a dose for phase 2.
results.quote: For both parts A and B, no serious adverse effects (AEs), discontinuation for AEs, or deaths were reported, and no clinically significant changes were observed for vital signs, electrocardiogram (ECG), or clinical laboratory evaluations.

results.finding: In phase 2 gonorrhea patients, 54/56 achieved microbiological cure after 3 g oral zoliflodacin.
results.detail: FDA described the phase 2 results as supportive. The primary endpoint was microbiological cure at the urogenital site.
results.quote:
The phase 2 trial results were supportive, with cure rates of 96.5% 
(55/57) and 96.4% (54/56) for the 2 g and 3 g zoliflodacin doses, respectively, compared to 
100% (28/28) for ceftriaxone.

results.finding: FDA approved one NDA for zoliflodacin oral suspension to treat uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea.
results.detail: The approval letter is electronically signed December 12, 2025; the package cover lists December 15, 2025 as the approval date. The record establishes an individual approval, not successive approvals from a specified platform.
